facts: The appellants have preferred this appeal against the dismissal of their petition u/s. 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code (for brevity 'Cr.P.C.') by the High Court of judicature for Rajasthan at Jodhpur.
Respondent No.2, Surendra Singhla, lodged a police case against the appellants as well as one Satish Singhla on 28.04.1998.

According to the averments and allegations in the written report, the informant is a partner of the Firm M/s. Rajshree Cotton Corporation, Sriganganagar, working as broker as well as dealer in the sale and purchase of cotton.
The appellants are Directors of M/s. R.P. Taxfab Limited, Modi Nagar, who purchased cotton through informant firm from time to time.
issues: Whether the FIR discloses a criminal offence or not
Whether the High Court was correct in dismissing the petition u/s. 482 of the Cr.P.C.
Whether the order of cognizance by the learned Magistrate is proper
petitioner_arguments: The FIR discloses only a civil case and there is no allegation or averment making out a criminal offence
The allegations and averments do not make out any criminal offence
The High Court should exercise its inherent jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding
respondent_arguments: There is merit in the contention that the FIR discloses a criminal offence
The allegations made in the FIR disclose commission of an offence
A second petition u/s. 482 of the Cr.P.C. can be entertained because order of Magistrate taking cognizance gives rise to a new cause of action
court_reasoning: If the complaint discloses only a simple case of civil dispute between the parties and there is an absolute absence of requisite averment to make out a case of cheating, the criminal proceeding can be quashed
The real test is whether the allegations in the complaint disclose a criminal offence or not
A given set of facts may make out a civil wrong as also a criminal offence
holding: The criminal proceedings against the appellants are not quashed
The order of cognizance by the learned Magistrate is upheld
